title: Why it made the number up, and what fixes it
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, experiments/logs.

blocks.text: So why did the model say 100? Trace the first digit back. When it wrote the one, it was looking back over 104 tokens.
blocks.say: So why did the model say one hundred? Trace the first digit back. When it wrote the one, it was looking back over one hundred and four tokens.

blocks.text: The only digits among them are the date: 26 October 2026. Nothing in the input carried Northbridge's stock. So the model did what it was trained to do. It wrote a plausible number.
blocks.say: The only digits among them are the date: twenty-six October, twenty twenty-six. Nothing in the input carried Northbridge's stock. So the model did what it was trained to do. It wrote a plausible number.

blocks.text: Now add one line to the prompt, straight from Ledgerline. BAT-500 at Manchester main stores: 5,400 on hand.
blocks.say: Now add one line to the prompt, straight from Ledgerline. BAT five hundred at Manchester main stores: five thousand four hundred on hand.

blocks.text: Same model, same question. This time the answer is 5,400. As it writes the five, block 10, head 13, puts 77 percent of its weight on the five tokens of that number.
blocks.say: Same model, same question. This time the answer is five thousand four hundred. As it writes the five, block ten, head thirteen, puts seventy-seven percent of its weight on the five tokens of that number.

blocks.text: The fix is not a bigger brain. It is the right facts, in front of it. Lecture 3 gives the model knowledge. Lecture 4 gives it tools.
blocks.say: The fix is not a bigger brain. It is the right facts, in front of it. Lecture three gives the model knowledge. Lecture four gives it tools.
